title: Critical local smoothing for the three-dimensional wave equation
main_claim: For every eps>0, ||Uf||_{L^3(R^3 x [1,2])} <= C_eps ||J^eps f||_{L^3(R^3)}, where U is the half-wave propagator. This is the critical p=3 case of Sogge's Euclidean local smoothing conjecture in 3D. By interpolation it gives the full range alpha > max(0, 1-3/p), and from that maximal half-wave, maximal and nonmaximal Bochner-Riesz, restriction and Kakeya-maximal consequences. The core input is Theorem 8.1 (round-cone exponent <= 100*eta), proved by contradiction using entropy and incidence arguments. That proof relies on the cylinder Theorem 2.x (exponent <= eta/2), Ren-Wang's Furstenberg theorem and the Guth-Wang-Zhang wave-envelope estimate.

issues.location: 10-bochner-riesz.tex, subsection Spherical restriction and Kakeya maximal estimates (eq:kakeya-maximal)
issues.description: The restriction-to-Kakeya step quotes the exponents for Wolff's Prop 4.1: restricted weak type (a,a) with a=r/(r-2) and norm h^{-2(3/a-1)}. I could not check these exponents against the cited source. The qualitative conclusion (an h^{-eps} loss as r decreases to 3) is the standard restriction-implies-Kakeya implication, so this is at most a bookkeeping point and does not touch the main theorem.
issues.evidence: "it first gives restricted weak type $(a,a)$, where $a=r/(r-2)<3$, with norm $O(h^{-2(3/a-1)})$ ... Interpolation with the trivial $L^\infty$ bound gives strong type $(3,3)$ with loss $h^{-2(1-a/3)}$"
